title.en: Your Role at a Shared Creative Table
title.zh: 共用创作桌：你会怎样交接这一页？

description.en: Six fictional workshop choices about work-in-progress labels, shared tools and asking what kind of feedback is wanted. Find your creative-table role.
description.zh: 六次虚构工作坊选择，标清进行中作品、共用工具、问明希望哪种反馈，发现你的共创桌角色。

introduction.en: Imagine a casual paper-craft table where several people leave work between sessions. You choose how to share materials and respond to drafts while keeping authorship and permission visible. This is a hobby scenario, not a workplace evaluation.
introduction.zh: 想象一张轻松纸艺桌，几个人在活动之间留着作品。你选择如何分享材料、回应草稿，也让作者与许可可见。这是爱好场景，不做职场评价。

focus.en: Making a creative handover clear through artifact labels, tool-sharing arrangements or feedback requested by the maker.
focus.zh: 通过作品标记、工具共用安排，或作者主动想要的反馈，让创作交接清楚。

prompt.en: An unfinished page is left on the common table. You…
prompt.zh: 未完成纸页留在共用桌上，你会……

label.en: Ask whose page it is and what state it should be kept in.
label.zh: 问作者是谁、希望怎样保留现状。

label.en: Move available common tools to a separate clear spot without editing the page.
label.zh: 不改纸页，把现成共用工具另放清楚位置。

label.en: Wait to offer comments until the maker says what feedback they want.
label.zh: 等作者说明想要什么反馈再评论。

prompt.en: Two people want the same tool. You…
prompt.zh: 两人都想用同一工具，你会……

label.en: Agree on a simple handover or turn for that item.
label.zh: 为这件物品约简单交接或轮次。

label.en: Mark the work that is waiting so nobody mistakes it for abandoned.
label.zh: 标记等待中的作品，避免误以为被放弃。

label.en: Ask whether a brief peer look would be useful while they wait.
label.zh: 问等待时是否想要一次简短同伴查看。

prompt.en: A maker says “what do you think?” about a draft. You first…
prompt.zh: 作者问草稿“你觉得怎样”，你先……

label.en: Ask which part they want you to respond to.
label.zh: 问希望你回应哪一部分。

label.en: Check which version they mean before discussing it.
label.zh: 讨论前确认指哪个版本。

label.en: Clear a place to lay it out without borrowing their personal tools.
label.zh: 腾一处可展开的位置，不擅借私人工具。

prompt.en: The session ends before the group’s project is finished. You…
prompt.zh: 活动结束，共同项目还没做完，你会……

label.en: Leave a short note on what is done and what is still open.
label.zh: 短记哪些已做、哪些仍开放。

label.en: Return shared items to the place agreed for next time.
label.zh: 把共用物归到已约下次使用处。

label.en: Ask whether the maker wants one comment now or a later review.
label.zh: 问作者现在想听一条，还是下次再看。

prompt.en: Someone suggests changing another person’s page. You…
prompt.zh: 有人建议修改另一人的纸页，你会……

label.en: Ask the maker whether editing or only commenting is welcome.
label.zh: 问作者欢迎直接修改还是只评论。

label.en: Keep the original state identifiable before any agreed change.
label.zh: 在任何已同意变动前，让原状态可辨。

label.en: Offer common materials for a separate trial version.
label.zh: 提供共用材料，另做试验版本。

prompt.en: What would make the table easy to return to?
prompt.zh: 怎样会让回到这张桌变容易？

label.en: Shared tools have a usable place and handover.
label.zh: 共用工具有好用的位置与交接。

label.en: Drafts clearly show their maker and current state.
label.zh: 草稿作者与当前状态清楚可见。

label.en: People know how to ask for and offer a bounded response.
label.zh: 大家知道怎样请求和提供有边界回应。

summary.en: Your shared table keeps the maker and the current state of a page visible. A small note can protect an unfinished idea from being mistaken for spare material. The portrait values a clear creative handover rather than a formal project-management identity.
summary.zh: 你的共用桌让纸页作者与当前状态可见。小便条能让未完想法不被误当备用材料。画像珍惜清楚创作交接，不授予正式项目管理身份。

example.en: You might leave “Mina’s trial layout, please keep as placed” beside a collage draft rather than expecting everybody to recognize which scraps are still in use.
example.zh: 你可能在拼贴草稿旁写“米娜试排中，请保留位置”，不期待人人认得哪些碎纸还在用。

strength.en: A legible state can reduce accidental changes and make it easier for someone to return without reconstructing what happened while they were away.
strength.zh: 可读状态能减少无意变动，也让人回来时不用重建离开期间发生过什么。

tradeoff.en: Labeling every tiny move can take over the creative session. A short note at a real handover point may be enough.
tradeoff.zh: 标记每个微动作也会接管创作时间。真正交接时一则短记，也许已够。

experiment.en: At the end of one shared creative session, leave a two-line note: whose work it is and what is open to change. Keep the note smaller than the work.
experiment.zh: 一次共同创作结束时，留两行：是谁的作品、哪些可改。让便条比作品本身小。

summary.en: Your table runs more easily when a tool can be found, used and returned without a small negotiation every time. You choose a practical handover that fits the activity. The result does not make you custodian of everyone’s belongings.
summary.zh: 工具不用每次都重新小协商，就能找到、使用、归还时，你的桌子更顺。你选择贴活动的实际交接。结果不让你保管所有人物品。

example.en: You might agree where the common ruler lives and how to pass it between two people working at the same table, while personal tools remain separately identified.
example.zh: 你可能约好共用尺放哪、两人怎样传递，也把个人工具分别标清。

strength.en: A simple sharing arrangement can prevent avoidable interruption and keep access to a common resource understandable for a newcomer.
strength.zh: 简单共用安排能减少无谓打断，也让新人明白怎样使用公共资源。

tradeoff.en: An overly fixed arrangement can fail when the project changes. Checking whether the actual users still find it helpful keeps the system modest.
tradeoff.zh: 项目变了，过度固定安排也会失效。问实际使用者是否仍有帮助，能让安排保持适度。

experiment.en: Choose one genuinely shared item and agree on its return place with its users. Avoid arranging somebody else’s personal materials without asking.
experiment.zh: 选一件确实共用物，与使用者约归位处。不问就安排他人私人材料的事可以省去。

summary.en: Your table gives a draft a response the maker actually asked for. A question about scope comes before a list of improvements. The ending values a bounded creative exchange, not a claim that your feedback is always correct or should always be followed.
summary.zh: 你的桌子给草稿作者实际想要的回应。先问范围，再列改进。结局珍惜有边界创作交换，不宣称你的反馈总正确或总该被采纳。

example.en: If a friend asks about a card design, you might check whether they want a first impression, a wording suggestion or help choosing between two versions.
example.zh: 朋友问卡片设计时，你可能先确认想听第一印象、文字建议，还是帮选两个版本。

strength.en: A clear feedback request can make a response more useful and let the maker retain ownership of the choices still being explored.
strength.zh: 清楚反馈请求让回应更有用，也让作者继续拥有仍在探索中选择的主导权。

tradeoff.en: Clarifying endlessly can postpone a small useful observation. Once the scope is clear enough, one concrete response may serve better than another round of questions.
tradeoff.zh: 澄清过久也会推迟有用小观察。范围足够明白后，一条具体回应可能比再问一轮更好。

experiment.en: Before commenting on a willing person’s draft, ask what kind of response would help. Offer one specific observation and leave the final choice with the maker.
experiment.zh: 评论愿意者草稿前，问哪种回应有帮助。给一条具体观察，让最终选择留在作者手里。
